paper_metadata.title: A HYBRID QUANTUM WASSERSTEIN GAN WITH APPLICATIONS TO OPTION PRICING

summary: The paper introduces a hybrid quantum Wasserstein GAN (qWGAN) for loading classical distributions into quantum states and integrates it with Iterative Quantum Amplitude Estimation for option pricing. Using a 5‑qubit generator (32-point discretization) trained for 2000 epochs, the Wasserstein model achieves relative entropy ≈0.0043 versus 0.1858 for a BCE baseline and estimates a European call payoff ≈0.166 compared to the true value 0.1618. Demonstrations include synthetic lognormal data, a Heston-model distribution, and Apple option data, but all experiments remain small-scale NISQ proofs of concept.

experiments.description: Hybrid qWGAN used to learn and load a lognormal distribution into a 5-qubit quantum generator, benchmarked against a BCE-loss qGAN baseline.

algorithm.variant: hybrid quantum Wasserstein GAN (quantum generator + classical discriminator)
algorithm.ansatz: Qiskit TwoLocal circuit with RX/RY rotation layers and shifted-circular-alternating CNOT entanglement
algorithm.convergence_criteria: trained for 2000 epochs; best result selected by relative entropy

problem_formulation.encoding_details: 5 qubits encode 32 discrete grid points for the target distribution; basis states map to values 0.0, 0.1, ..., 3.1
problem_formulation.objective_function: minimize Wasserstein-1 distance between generated and target distributions; generator minimizes E_fake[D(x)] while discriminator maximizes E_real[D(x)] - E_fake[D(x)]
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: none reported beyond Wasserstein training objective

problem_instance.description: Load a discretized lognormal distribution for option-pricing use case

dataset_specification.description: Lognormal(mu = ln(1.1) - 0.25^2/2, sigma = 0.25); rounded to one decimal place; support mapped to 0.0 to 3.1 on 32 grid points

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: sample 10000 points from lognormal distribution; round to one decimal place; discretize onto 32-point grid; no scaling needed
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: compare BCE vs Wasserstein setups after 2000 epochs; report relative entropy and Wasserstein distance; select best result with lowest relative entropy

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: generate and discretize lognormal training data; build classical discriminator in PyTorch
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: compute relative entropy and Wasserstein distance; compare generated distribution to target

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: oscillatory but convergent; Wasserstein setup more stable than BCE

speedup_claims.conditions: loading arbitrary distributions into n qubits
speedup_claims.caveats: Claim is for distribution loading complexity, not end-to-end option pricing runtime.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O(poly(n)) for distribution loading via qGAN-style loading channel
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: O(2^n) for prior state-preparation method referenced in the paper

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Would require scalable qGAN training circuits for large n where classical state preparation scales as O(2^n); current experiment uses only 5 qubits.
limiting_factors: Experiment performed only on simulator with 5 qubits
No runtime comparison with classical distribution learning
Training instability and barren plateau issues for larger QNNs

notes: hardware.type reported from 'aer_simulator' in numerical results; num_qubits reported as 5 qubits for the generator; circuit depth not explicitly stated, but 2-layer TwoLocal ansatz is reported so depth was not numerically reconstructed.
The paper explicitly contrasts O(poly(n)) qGAN loading with prior O(2^n) loading methods.
Paper claims improved scaling (O(poly(n)) vs O(2^n)) for distribution loading but provides only small simulator experiments without runtime benchmarking.

experiments.description: Hybrid qWGAN used to price a European call option by loading the learned lognormal distribution, applying an ancilla-based payoff circuit, and estimating the payoff with IQAE on real IBM hardware.

algorithm.variant: Iterative Quantum Amplitude Estimation (IQAE) within a three-step option-pricing pipeline
algorithm.convergence_criteria: IQAE run to estimate payoff amplitude; qWGAN training separately run for 2000 epochs

problem_formulation.encoding_details: 5-qubit discretized distribution loaded into state; 2 ancilla qubits used for payoff and amplitude estimation
problem_formulation.objective_function: estimate E[max(ST-K,0)] via amplitude of ancilla qubit |1>
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: comparator circuit marks states with ST > K; linear payoff rotation maps payoff to ancilla amplitude

problem_instance.description: European call option pricing on synthetic lognormal asset-price distribution

dataset_specification.description: strike K = 1.0; distribution from synthetic lognormal training set

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: load trained 5-qubit distribution; comparator circuit for strike; payoff rotation on ancilla
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: compare target distribution payoff, trained distribution payoff, and IQAE-estimated value; report 99% confidence interval

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: train qWGAN on synthetic lognormal data; discretize distribution; construct comparator and payoff circuits
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: convert measured ancilla probability to option payoff estimate; compute confidence interval
implementation_details.total_execution_time: about 20 minutes on ibm_nairobi (queue time dominates)

speedup_claims.conditions: amplitude estimation / IQAE for option payoff estimation
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper reports the quadratic error-scaling advantage; the wall-clock run on IBM hardware is dominated by queue time.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: quadratic error scaling in IQAE, O(1/M) amplitude-estimation error scaling

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Fault‑tolerant circuits capable of large‑scale amplitude estimation with many qubits and low noise; large sample sizes to exploit O(1/ε) scaling.
limiting_factors: Quadratic speedup insufficient to offset fault‑tolerant overhead
Hybrid classical training overhead for qWGAN

notes: The paper explicitly states the option-pricing evaluation was executed on ibm_nairobi and that 2 ancilla qubits were used; with 5 generator qubits this implies 7 total qubits.
The paper does not report a numeric circuit depth for the full pricing circuit, so that field is null.
Paper claims quadratic Monte Carlo speedup via amplitude estimation (1/ε vs 1/ε²) but experiments are small NISQ demonstrations and do not outperform classical Monte Carlo in practice.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: reuse trained qWGAN distribution; build digital payoff circuit
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: estimate digital payoff and confidence interval from measured ancilla probabilities

speedup_claims.caveats: The paper states the estimate is only about 1% below the true value; no explicit classical runtime comparison is given.

limiting_factors: Digital payoff experiment still uses same 5‑qubit toy distribution
